To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) price supports are costly to the Polish economy, (ii) price supports improve the position of Polish farmers relative to nonfarmers only if quantity controls are in place, and (iii) the best policy for Polish agriculture is to avoid price supports and instead promote structural adjustment.

the most efficient and least costly agricultural policy for Poland is one that promotes efficiency, adjustment to the new economic environment, and structural change in Polish agriculture, and that this policy is not a Common Agricultural Policy-type policy.

(1) Poland should not introduce price supports in agriculture; (2) the most efficient agricultural strategy is to promote efficiency, structural change and adjustment to the market environment; (3) the best strategy is to avoid price supports in agriculture before Poland joins the Common Agricultural Policy; and (4) in the interim, policies that reduce the number of farm jobs are most appropriate.
